claim: Intercommunication Enhancements may become state of the art in agent orchestration if controlled evaluation demonstrates reproducible architecture-specific gains in reliability, recovery, provenance, authority integrity, long-horizon task success and cost-adjusted performance over strong same-model baselines.
candidate_lessons: Kernel quality should be validated before large swarm scale because scaling can amplify coordination errors as well as useful work.
Hallucination tolerance should be measured as fault containment and evidence-promotion control rather than as an expectation of zero hallucinations.
Fresh-agent continuity should depend on durable state reconstruction and provenance rather than inaccessible conversational memory.
Authority boundaries should be enforced outside model-generated language.
Cumulative swarm intelligence requires evidence-gated learning promotion.
State-of-the-art is an empirical measurement claim, not an architectural self-description.

external_evidence.source: Anthropic - How we built our multi-agent research system
external_evidence.relevance: Reports 90.2% internal multi-agent research improvement over a single-agent configuration and large token-budget effects; supports resource-normalized evaluation.

Long-horizon 108-workflow benchmark with average 318 tool calls in a reported configuration and 20.6% best primary binary completion; failure modes overlap with state-recovery and constraint-retention targets.

external_evidence.source: OpenAI - Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities
external_evidence.relevance: Demonstrates benchmark contamination/evaluator-quality risk and supports held-out, uncontaminated, independently reproduced evaluation.

confidence.meaning: The evaluation logic and external motivation are strong enough to justify a research program, but no controlled project benchmark has yet established a SOTA result.

scope: agent orchestration, intercommunication, long-horizon reliability, swarm hardening and evaluation methodology
